title: Man. Post. Cap. VIII: penalties via Adam's communicated malice; leaven of the mass
pass_a_gloss: He did the opposite instead. Why, unless so we grasp that the pains fixed in that sentence touch us only because Adam shared them with us—his sin's desert-making malice passed along by fleshly generation? Seek the reason we suffer those pains not in God charging us with a deed we never did so he may punish us, but in Adam alone and in that sin's nature: like yeast worked into the dough of humankind it spoiled the whole loaf not by divine imputation but by fleshly generation, and tainted it with malice. Placeus is defending God's cause—please do not fight him.
pass_b_english: But now he did the Contrary—to what end, unless that we understand the penalties decreed by that sentence do not pertain to us, except because Adam communicated them with us, the malice of his sin which merits them having been communicated through carnal generation? and so that we should not seek the cause why we pay those penalties in God imputing to us an action which we in no way committed, that he may punish us, but in Adam alone, and in the nature of the sin itself, which, like some leaven put into the mass of the human race, corrupted that whole mass not through God's imputation but through carnal generation, and infected it with malice. You see that I am pleading God's cause; do not, I beg you, oppose him.
source_text: Nunc autem Contrarium fecit, quorsum, nisi ut intelligamus decretas ea sententia poenas ad nos non pertinere, nisi quia Adamus nobiscum eas communicavit, communicata, quae illas meretur, per carnalem generationem peccati sui malitia? atque ita causam cur eas poenas luamus, non quaeramus in Deo nobis actionem, quam nullo modo commisimus, imputante, ut nos puniat, sed in Adamo solo, & natura peccati ipsius, quod, ut fermentum quoddam massae generis humani immissum, eam totam, non per Dei imputationem, sed per carnalem generationem corrupit, ac malitia infecit. Vides me Dei causam agere, noli quaeso ei adversari.
